m.d: If something is odd, it is not normal and usually you don't like it or don't understand it.
m.e: The neighbours thought him very odd, because he would leave his doors open all night.

m.d: The odd time, drink, problem, etc. is one that happens sometimes, but not often.
m.e: I don't really drink – just the odd beer at the weekend.

m.d: An odd sock, boot, etc. is one without its pair.
m.e: The clown was wearing odd socks.

m.d: In statistics, the odds are the chance something will happen divided by the chance it will not happen:
The odds of something happening are the chances it will happen.
m.e: I don't like the odds here.

m.d: To do something oddly is to do it in an odd manner.
Something's odor is its smell, usually a bad smell.
m.e: The football players had an odor after their match, and I had to hold my breath as they walked past.

m.d: A long adventurous journey or trip.
m.e: The odyssey of Odysseus was written down by Homer in his epic poem, the Odyssey.

m.d: An intellectual or spiritual journey or quest.
